div.p: Visual Studio Code's settings let you tailor your working environment to fit requirements for specific languages or extensions, or to suit your own preferences.

A general guide to settings is provided by the Visual Studio Code documentation: User and Workspace Settings. This page lists the XSLT/XPath extension's own settings, and the editor settings of most interest for XSLT and XPath.

From the Command Palette (⇧⌘P) you can either invoke Preferences: Open User Settings or Preferences: Open Workspace Settings. Editor settings can also be applied in a language-specific way: for this, use the command Preferences: Configure Language Specific Settings.

Settings are either edited in the Settings form or in a JSON editor. Open the JSON editor by clicking the Open Settings (JSON) button at the top right of the Editor Group. This opens the corresponding settings.json file directly.

User settings apply wherever you use VS Code, so they suit paths on your own computer, such as the Saxon jar. Workspace settings are saved in the project's .vscode/settings.json and apply to everyone who opens the project, so they suit settings a team shares, such as an XML catalog or XSLT packages.

To list the extension's settings in the Settings editor, type XSLT in its search box. All of them are listed below, with their defaults. The sections after the tables describe the most important ones.

tr.td: The path of your Saxon jar file, needed to run or debug stylesheets with SaxonJ - see The Saxon jar.
The processor Quick Run uses: "xslt" (SaxonJ), "xslt-js" (SaxonJS) or "xslt-c" (SaxonC). Switching processor in Quick Run saves the choice here.
Offer SaxonJ (xslt) tasks - see Task types.
Offer SaxonJS (xslt-js) tasks.
Offer SaxonC (xslt-c) tasks.
The folder containing the SaxonC command-line executable (Transform or Transform.exe) - see SaxonC tasks.
The path of SaxonC's saxon-license.lic file, passed to SaxonC as --licenseFileLocation: - see Licensing.
More folders to search for SaxonC's native libraries. The lib folder beside the executable is always included - see Native library path.
The path of the nu.validator htmlparser jar, added to SaxonJ's classpath for XSLT 4.0 stylesheets, for Saxon's parse-html() function.
When debugging, open the output written so far beside the stylesheet, at the first pause where there is some - see Output while debugging.
An OASIS XML catalog file, for resolving the href of xsl:import and xsl:include - also passed to Saxon - see XML catalog.
The files for xsl:use-package names - see XSLT packages.

For a module that another stylesheet imports or includes, find that stylesheet from the workspace's files, so references to its declarations are resolved without opening it first - see Inferred imports.

Completion of element and attribute names in XPath: "latest" suggests the names that can occur at that point in the path, from the XML context file; "none" suggests the names already used in the stylesheet - see IntelliSense for XPath locations.

Prefixes of functions the processor provides, such as Java extension functions - calls of functions with these prefixes aren't checked. The quick fix for a function that isn't found adds its prefix - see Java extension functions.
Allow XSLT 4.0 named item types and xsl:note in XSLT 3.0 stylesheets, for Saxon PE and EE 12.8 or later - see below.

div.p: To run or debug stylesheets with SaxonJ - Saxon for Java - set XSLT.tasks.saxonJar to the full path of your Saxon jar file, usually as a user setting, since the path is specific to your computer. Any Saxon edition works, including Saxon-HE. The Debugger needs Saxon 12 or later, and a Java runtime must be on the PATH:
On Windows, write each \ in the path as \\, as JSON requires - e.g. "C:\\saxon\\saxon-he-12.9.jar". For Saxon-PE or Saxon-EE, keep the licence file, saxon-license.lic, in the same folder as the jar.
XSLT tasks refer to the setting as ${config:XSLT.tasks.saxonJar}. For downloading Saxon and Java, see SaxonJ tasks.

Packages in the workspace are found without a setting. For a package outside the workspace, add its path to XSLT.resources.xsltPackages - its name and version are read from its xsl:package element. See XSLT Packages.

To resolve the href of xsl:import and xsl:include - and the URIs of fixed-namespaces - with an OASIS XML catalog, and pass the catalog to Saxon when a stylesheet is run, set XSLT.resources.catalog to the catalog file's path, relative to the workspace folder. See XML Catalogs.

The extension provides a task type for each Saxon processor - xslt for SaxonJ, xslt-js for SaxonJS and xslt-c for SaxonC - and all three are enabled by default. To stop a processor's tasks being offered, for example in Run Build Task, turn off its setting:
See Tasks for configuring each task type.
div.h4: XSLT 4.0 Item Types and Notes in XSLT 3.0
div.p: Saxon PE and EE 12.8 or later, run with syntax extensions, accept XSLT 4.0's named item types and xsl:note in a stylesheet with version="3.0". To edit such stylesheets with the same support as for XSLT 4.0, enable the setting XSLT.validation.xslt30ItemTypesAndNotes - it's off by default. For a team, add it to the workspace settings, in the project's .vscode/settings.json:
With the setting, in an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet:

ul.li: xsl:item-type declarations are accepted, with record(...) and enum(...) types - which can also be used directly in as attributes
the record and enumeration type support applies: completions of record fields, map keys and enumeration values, checks of map constructors, lookups and values, hover help, and renaming a record field
xsl:note needs no use-when attribute - see Code Documentation

div.p: Other XSLT 4.0 and XPath 4.0 features - such as xsl:switch, keyword arguments and fn(...) types - still need version="4.0", and are reported as errors in an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet.

Without the setting, xsl:item-type and record and enumeration types are reported as errors in an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet, and an xsl:note gets a warning unless it's excluded with use-when="false()", as an XSLT 3.0 processor reports XTSE0010 for it.

To run the stylesheets, Saxon needs syntax extensions: the --allowSyntaxExtensions:on option on the command line, or allowSyntaxExtensions="true" in a Saxon configuration file. The extension's XSLT tasks and Quick Run enable it with the default "allowSyntaxExtensions40": "auto" task property, for Saxon PE and EE.

Saxon's earlier syntax for named types - saxon:type-alias, tuple(...) types and ~name for a reference to a type alias - is ignored by Saxon 12.8 and later, which only report the references. The linter warns about a saxon:type-alias, and the command XSLT: Convert Saxon Type Aliases to xsl:item-type - also the warning's quick fix - converts them in all the workspace's files, shown for review in the refactor preview first:

ul.li: tuple(t: xs:integer, label?: xs:string) becomes record(t as xs:integer, label? as xs:string)

div.p: A type alias with an extensible tuple type, e.g. tuple(a: xs:string, *), isn't converted - nor is one that references it - as XSLT 4.0 has no extensible record types. These are listed after the conversion, to convert by hand.
div.h4: Default Editor Settings for XSLT, XPath and XML
div.p: The extension sets these VS Code editor settings for the xslt, xpath and xml languages - for .xsl, .xslt, .xpath and XML files. As they're set for each language, they don't affect files in other languages. Any of them can be changed in a language-specific setting, e.g. "[xslt]": { "editor.tabSize": 4 } - see Creating User and Workspace Settings.

tr.td: This extension formats the file - see Code Formatting.
Lines are indented as you type, e.g. a new line, or a closing tag.
Pasted text is indented to fit where it's pasted.
The file isn't formatted when it's saved.
If formatOnSave is turned on, the whole file is formatted - or only the lines changed, with "modifications".
The number of spaces for each level of indentation.
Indentation uses spaces, not tabs.
For an existing file, the tab size and spaces or tabs are detected from its content, instead of the two settings above.
Unlike VS Code's default, - and . aren't word separators, so double-clicking selects a whole name, such as current-group - see Word Separators.
Syntax highlighting for XSLT and XPath, which uses semantic tokens - see Syntax Highlighting. It's also set for the xsl language.
The Outline view doesn't show arrays - see Code Navigation.

div.p: The extension also defines how the editor treats XSLT files in ways that aren't settings, so they can't be changed:

ul.li: Comments - Toggle Block Comment (⇧⌥A) wraps the selection in <!-- and -->. In .xpath files it uses XPath's (: and :).
Auto-closing - typing {, [, (, a quote or a backtick adds the closing character. So does &, which adds ; for an entity reference, and (:, which adds : to start an XPath comment.
Surrounding - typing one of these characters with text selected surrounds the selection with the pair, e.g. selecting $total and typing ( gives ($total).

Words - a prefixed name such as xsl:template, a variable reference such as $total-price, and an attribute name test such as @select each count as one word - for example, when VS Code finds the word at the cursor for word-based suggestions.
Folding regions - <?region?> and <?endregion?> processing instructions mark a region that can be folded - see Folding.

div.p: The editor.wordSeparators setting affects how the full 'word' is selected when you double-click on a part of the word. The characters listed are used as word separators. Typically in XSLT, you do not want characters like - and . treated as word separators, as these characters are valid within a QName like an attribute name or a variable name.

Visual Studio Code's Agents window only runs the extensions on a list chosen by Microsoft, and the XSLT/XPath extension isn't on it yet - so, there, XSLT files have plain XML highlighting, with none of the extension's features.
